caveats: Q4 gross profit and revenue are derived by subtracting the nine-month year-to-date figures (through March 31, 2026) from the full-year FY2026 figures. They are not reported directly as standalone quarterly values.
The gross margin is my own arithmetic on those two derived values (60,482,000,000 / 90,007,000,000). It is about 67.197%, shown as roughly 67.2% in the text.
No filing passages were provided, so this answer gives no management commentary on margin drivers.

claims.text: Microsoft's gross profit for fiscal Q4 2026 was about $60.48 billion. This is a derived value: FY2026 gross profit of $225.465 billion minus the nine-month figure of $164.983 billion.
Microsoft's revenue for fiscal Q4 2026 was about $90.01 billion. This is a derived value: FY2026 revenue of $331.839 billion minus the nine-month figure of $241.832 billion.
Gross margin = gross profit / revenue = 60,482,000,000 / 90,007,000,000 ≈ 0.67197, or about 67.2%.

raw_output.summary: Microsoft's gross margin in fiscal Q4 2026 (April 1 to June 30, 2026) was about 67.2%. That is derived gross profit of $60.482 billion divided by derived revenue of $90.007 billion.
